answer: Retrospective activity-correlation screening. Agents’ action logs are periodically clustered by timing and content overlap; a sybil tide shows up as many identities sharing one faint behavioral fingerprint. Flagged clusters lose earned reputation and future task access. To survive, an attacker must give each identity genuinely distinct history, multiplying setup and maintenance cost per agent across the nebula of accounts. Honest idiosyncrasy stays cheap; forged diversity is expensive, and the lagoon of shared patterns exposes it.
